subject: Brightwell Property Group manages 40 buildings and has used the same elevator-maintenance vendor for six years at a rate of $1,450 per unit per month. A newer vendor has quoted $1,180 per unit per month for the same service scope, and Brightwell has not yet checked references or reviewed the new vendor's incident-response times, which the current vendor has met within a 2-hour SLA for six years without a missed call. Elevator downtime is also a life-safety and compliance issue in occupied residential buildings, not just an operating cost, so a slower response time on a callout carries risk beyond the monthly invoice. The team is deciding whether to switch vendors outright, run a side-by-side pilot on a subset of buildings first, or renegotiate with the current vendor using the new quote as leverage, and has not yet reached a recommendation.
question: Since we'd save over $250 per unit every month, why wouldn't we just switch to the cheaper vendor right away?
why: The question treats cost as the only relevant axis and frames an immediate switch as the default, ignoring the unverified SLA and reference risk stated in the subject.
